## Overview

Adds `--all2all-backend mori`, an expert-parallel all2all backend that runs MoRI EPv2 (`mori.ops.dispatch_combine_v2`) where it is supported and MoRI EPv1 otherwise. EPv2 dispatches and combines tokens through a MoRI CCO symmetric-memory window, so all EP ranks must sit in one load/store-accessible (LSA) team, e.g. one node.

`VLLM_MORI_EP_V2` selects the version. Unset, `mori` prefers EPv2 and falls back to EPv1 with a warning when the EP size exceeds 8 (except on gfx1250, whose UALink team can span hosts), `MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1`, `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`, or a non-BF16 model. `1` forces EPv2 and `0` selects EPv1. The choice is made once in the ROCm platform's config hook. On EPv1 across nodes, `mori` uses InterNodeV1LL when the per-rank token budget is at most `VLLM_MORI_DISPATCH_INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH_THRESHOLD` (default 256), and InterNodeV1 otherwise.

The existing MoRI backends (`mori_high_throughput`, `mori_low_latency`) are unchanged and always run EPv1.

## Claims

- On DeepSeek-V4-Pro with DP8+EP8 on 8× MI355X, `mori` on EPv2 matches TP8 and the existing MoRI EP backend on GSM8K and gives about 3.9× the output throughput of `mori_high_throughput`.
- Triton MoE: `TritonExperts.moe_sum` now skips unrouted (`-1`) top-k slots whenever `topk_ids` is given, not only under an `expert_map`; the alignment never computes those slots, so their scratch rows were summed unwritten. Dynamic per-tensor FP8/INT8 also clears that scratch first, so the unwritten rows do not enter the shared activation scale.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 8× MI355X, `--moe-backend aiter`, CUDA graphs, MoRI main.

| Backend | Parallelism | GSM8K (lm-eval, 1319 q, 5-shot, strict) | Output tok/s (random 1k/1k, c64) |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | TP8 | 0.950 | — |
| `mori_high_throughput` | DP8+EP8 | 0.958 | 530 |
| `mori` (EPv2) | DP8+EP8 | 0.955 | 2054 |

GSM8K ran with 4096 max new tokens, so about 33 answers per backend were cut off before the final answer. Absolute scores are lower than with a longer budget, but the backends are comparable to each other. The eager mode (`--enforce-eager`) start-up also passed.

[P1] Broadcast the CCO unique ID from the EP group's rank 0

`self.rank` above is group-local, but `src=0` here denotes global rank 0. With PP=2, DP=2, TP=1 on a single node, the EP groups are `[0, 2]` and `[1, 3]`. +### MoRI EP (ROCm)
+
+`--all2all-backend mori` moves MoE tokens with MoRI. It runs MoRI EPv2 (`mori.ops.dispatch_combine_v2`, which reads and writes peer GPU memory directly through a MoRI CCO symmetric-memory window) where EPv2 is supported, and MoRI EPv1 otherwise.
+
+```bash
+VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
+VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
+vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+    --data-parallel-size 8 \
+    --enable-expert-parallel \
+    --all2all-backend mori
+```
+
+`VLLM_MORI_EP_V2` selects the MoRI version:
+
+| `VLLM_MORI_EP_V2` | Behavior |
+| ----------------- | -------- |
+| unset | EPv2, falling back to EPv1 with a warning when the EP size exceeds 8 (except on gfx1250, whose UALink team can span hosts), `MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1`, `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe`, or a non-BF16 model |
+| `1` | Always EPv2. The checks above only log a warning; startup fails if the EP ranks are not in one CCO-LSA team |
+| `0` | EPv1 |
+
+On EPv1, `mori` uses the IntraNode kernel within one node. Across nodes it uses InterNodeV1LL when the per-rank token budget (`--max-num-batched-tokens`) is at most `VLLM_MORI_DISPATCH_INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH_THRESHOLD` (default 256), and InterNodeV1 otherwise. `mori_high_throughput` and `mori_low_latency` always run EPv1 and pin the inter-node kernel to InterNodeV1 and InterNodeV1LL respectively.
+
+EPv2 limitations:
+
+- All EP ranks must be in one MoRI CCO-LSA team, i.e. GPUs that can load and store each other's memory: one node, or one UALink fabric. Startup fails otherwise; there is no multi-node RDMA path yet.
+- Activations are dispatched in BF16, so the model dtype must be BF16 and the experts must take unquantized inputs (AITER fused MoE, which quantizes after the all-to-all, or BF16 experts). Experts that expect activations quantized before dispatch, such as FP8 or INT8 Triton experts, are rejected at startup.
+- AITER shared-expert fusion is not supported: set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0`.
+- Install a MoRI build that ships `mori.ops.dispatch_combine_v2`. On NICs that limit a registered memory region to 2 GiB, the window registration fails once the dispatch arena outgrows that limit (DeepSeek-V4-Pro at EP8 already does at the default 16k batched tokens).
+- Older MoRI builds leave a stale HIP error behind when the fabric-handle probe fails (e.g. on a single MI355X node), and the next PyTorch allocation raises `operation not supported`.
+
 ## Multi-Node Deployment
 
 For multi-node deployment, use the DeepEP communication kernel with one of two modes (see [Backend Selection Guide](#backend-selection-guide) above).

+"""MORI EPv2 prepare/finalize and all2all manager, with MORI faked out."""
+
+import sys
+from datetime import timedelta
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import Mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+
+import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.mori_epv2 as mori_epv2
+from vllm.config.parallel import resolve_mori_all2all
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.mori_epv2 import (
+    MoriEPv2PrepareAndFinalize,
+)
+from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port
+
+
+class FakeOp:
+    """MORI EPv2 op whose receive buffers have `capacity` rows, `recv` valid."""
+
+    def __init__(self, capacity=256, recv=0):
+        self.routing = object()
+        self.recv_a1 = torch.full((capacity, 4), float("nan"), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        self.recv_weights = torch.full((capacity, 2), float("inf"))
+        self.recv_ids = torch.full((capacity, 2), 5, dtype=torch.int32)
+        self.recv = recv
+        self.combine_in = torch.empty(capacity, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        self.sent_ids: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        self.combine_input: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        self.combine_routing = None
+
+    def combine_in_view(self):
+        return self.combine_in
+
+    def dispatch(self, input, weights, scales, indices, *, return_routing=True):
+        self.sent_ids = indices
+        return (
+            self.recv_a1,
+            self.recv_weights,
+            None,
+            self.recv_ids,
+            torch.tensor([self.recv], dtype=torch.int32),
+            self.routing,
+        )
+
+    def combine(self, input, weights=None, indices=None, *, routing):
+        self.combine_input = input
+        self.combine_routing = routing
+        return torch.zeros(1, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16), None
+
+
+def _make_pf(op, num_local_experts=2, rank_expert_offset=0):
+    return MoriEPv2PrepareAndFinalize(op, 16, 4, num_local_experts, rank_expert_offset)
+
+
+def _run(monkeypatch, op, num_tokens_across_dp, topk_ids, **pf_kwargs):
+    """One prepare + finalize round trip under the given DP token counts."""
+    if num_tokens_across_dp is None:
+        ctx = SimpleNamespace(dp_metadata=None)
+    else:
+        counts = torch.tensor(num_tokens_across_dp)
+        ctx = SimpleNamespace(
+            dp_metadata=SimpleNamespace(num_tokens_across_dp_cpu=counts)
+        )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mori_epv2, "is_forward_context_available", lambda: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mori_epv2, "get_forward_context", lambda: ctx)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        mori_epv2, "get_dp_group", lambda: SimpleNamespace(rank_in_group=0)
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "is_current_stream_capturing", lambda: False)
+    prepare_finalize = _make_pf(op, **pf_kwargs)
+    num_tokens = topk_ids.shape[0]
+    prepared = prepare_finalize.prepare(
+        torch.ones(num_tokens, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+        torch.ones(num_tokens, 2, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+        topk_ids,
+        num_experts=8,
+        expert_map=None,
+        apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
+        quant_config=SimpleNamespace(is_per_tensor=False, a1_scale=None),
+    )
+    prepare_finalize.finalize(
+        torch.empty(num_tokens, 4, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+        prepared[0],
+        prepared[4],
+        prepared[3],
+        False,
+        SimpleNamespace(),
+    )
+    return prepared
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "num_tokens_across_dp,recv,rows",
+    [
+        # Sum of DP batches (6) rounded up to 32 rows, of 256 capacity rows.
+        ([1, 3, 2, 0], 7, 32),
+        ([33, 0, 0, 0], 20, 64),
+        # TP=2 per DP rank: each TP rank may send its DP batch, 2 * 50 rows.
+        ([30, 20], 90, 128),
+        # Dispatchers not a multiple of DP ranks: dispatchers * largest batch.
+        ([10, 20, 5], 60, 96),
+        # Bound above capacity: keep the full buffer.
+        ([100, 100, 100, 100], 200, 256),
+        # No DP metadata, or stale metadata missing this rank's batch: full buffer.
+        (None, 7, 256),
+        ([0, 3, 2, 0], 5, 256),
+    ],
+)
+def test_receive_rows_are_bounded_by_dp_tokens(
+    monkeypatch, num_tokens_across_dp, recv, rows
+):
+    op = FakeOp(recv=recv)
+    a1, _, meta, ids, weights = _run(
+        monkeypatch, op, num_tokens_across_dp, torch.tensor([[0, 1]])
+    )
+    for t, buf in ((a1, op.recv_a1), (ids, op.recv_ids), (weights, op.recv_weights)):
+        assert t.shape[0] == rows
+        assert t.data_ptr() == buf.data_ptr()  # views, no copy
+    # Rows past the receive count are cleared; rows past the bound are untouched.

+            # Metadata that does not cover this rank's own batch is stale; a
+            # bound derived from it could cut off received rows.
+            logger.debug_once(

+                "using the full receive buffer."
+            )
+            return capacity
+        if n_dp > 0 and self.num_dispatchers_ % n_dp == 0:
+            bound = self.num_dispatchers_ // n_dp * int(tokens.sum())
+        else:
+            bound = self.num_dispatchers_ * int(tokens.max())
+        bound = max(bound, 1)
+        bound = -(-bound // _RECV_ROW_ALIGN) * _RECV_ROW_ALIGN

+
+    def prepare(
+        self,
+        a1: torch.Tensor,
+        topk_weights: torch.Tensor,
+        topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        num_experts: int,
+        expert_map: torch.Tensor | None,
+        apply_router_weight_on_input: bool,
+        quant_config: FusedMoEQuantConfig,
+        defer_input_quant: bool = False,
+    ) -> mk.PrepareResultType:
+        del num_experts, expert_map, defer_input_quant
+        assert not apply_router_weight_on_input, (
+            "MORI EPv2 does not support apply_router_weight_on_input=True"
+        )
+        if a1.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+            raise ValueError(f"MORI EPv2 requires BF16 dispatch input, got {a1.dtype}")
+
+        (
+            dispatch_a1,
+            dispatch_weights,
+            dispatch_scale,
+            dispatch_ids,
+            dispatch_recv_token_num,
+            self._routing,
+        ) = self.mori_op.dispatch(
+            a1,
+            topk_weights.to(torch.float32),
+            None,
+            self._route_padding_locally(topk_ids.to(torch.int32)),
+            return_routing=True,
+        )
+        rows = self._recv_rows_bound(a1, dispatch_a1.shape[0])
+        if rows < dispatch_a1.shape[0]:
+            dispatch_a1 = dispatch_a1[:rows]
+            dispatch_weights = dispatch_weights[:rows]
+            dispatch_ids = dispatch_ids[:rows]
+            if dispatch_scale is not None:
+                dispatch_scale = dispatch_scale[:rows]
+        # MORI reuses capacity-sized buffers without clearing unused rows.
+        unused = (
+            torch.arange(dispatch_a1.shape[0], device=dispatch_a1.device)
+            >= dispatch_recv_token_num

+        if not self._experts_read_recv_rows_only or (

+            dispatch_a1.masked_fill_(unused, 0)
+        dispatch_weights.masked_fill_(unused, 0)
+        dispatch_ids.masked_fill_(unused, -1)
+        expert_tokens_meta = mk.ExpertTokensMetadata(
+            expert_num_tokens=dispatch_recv_token_num,
+            expert_num_tokens_cpu=None,
+        )
+        return (
+            dispatch_a1,
+            dispatch_scale,
+            expert_tokens_meta,
+            dispatch_ids,
+            dispatch_weights,
+        )

+        topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        apply_router_weight_on_input: bool,

+        del topk_weights, topk_ids, apply_router_weight_on_input
+        del weight_and_reduce_impl

[P1] Broadcast the CCO unique ID from the EP group's rank 0

`self.rank` above is group-local, but `src=0` here denotes global rank 0. With PP=2, DP=2, TP=1 on a single node, the EP groups are `[0, 2]` and `[1, 3]`. The second stage generates its UID on global rank 1, then this broadcast raises `ValueError: Global rank 0 is not part of group`, preventing startup even though each EP group fits within one LSA team.

Please use `group_src=0`, or translate group-local rank 0 to its global rank before passing `src`. I reproduced this by executing this method with four CPU/Gloo processes and a mocked CCO communicator; the original fails on ranks 1 and 3, while `group_src=0` passes on all four. The current manager test mocks out `broadcast_object_list`, so it does not catch this subgroup case.
